claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy is homogeneous and contains no secondary oxide dispersoids.
Powder metallurgy can produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale Y2O3 particles in the alloy matrix.
The introduced Y2O3 particles will remain uniformly distributed at grain boundaries.
The introduced Y2O3 particles will remain uniformly distributed within grains.
The nanoscale Y2O3 particles will be thermally stable under the stated conditions.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles obstruct dislocation motion in the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by Y2O3 particles provides dispersion strengthening.
Y2O3 dispersion strengthening will increase yield strength relative to an alloy without dispersoids.
Y2O3 dispersion strengthening will increase hardness relative to an alloy without dispersoids.
The strengthening will not compromise the alloy's thermal stability under the stated conditions.
The strengthening will not compromise the alloy's irradiation resistance under the stated conditions.
The predicted improvement should hold above approximately 1000 degrees Celsius under moderate reactor-relevant irradiation exposure.
Particle aggregation or inhomogeneous dispersion will diminish the strengthening effect.
Extreme irradiation doses or temperatures substantially above the design range may cause particle coarsening.
Particle aggregation or coarsening may cause local softening.
